definitions.ART: The conscious production or arrangement of sounds, colours, forms, movements, or other elements in a manner that affects the senses and emotions, usually specifically the production of the beautiful in a graphic or plastic medium.
definitions.DRAW: The result of a contest that neither side has won; a tie.
definitions.PAINT: A substance that is applied as a liquid or paste, and dries into a solid coating that protects or adds color/colour to an object or surface to which it has been applied.
definitions.READ: A reading or an act of reading, especially an actor's part of a play.
definitions.WRITE: The act or style of writing.
definitions.SING: A gathering at which people sing songs.
definitions.DANCE: A sequence of rhythmic steps or movements usually performed to music, for pleasure or as a form of social interaction.
definitions.BAKE: The act of cooking food by baking.
definitions.SEW: To use a needle to pass thread repeatedly through (pieces of fabric) in order to join them together.
definitions.SWIM: An act or instance of swimming.
definitions.BIKE: A vehicle that has two wheels, one behind the other, a steering handle, and a saddle seat or seats and is usually propelled by the action of a rider’s feet upon pedals.
definitions.CAMP: An outdoor place acting as temporary accommodation in tents or other temporary structures.
definitions.FISH: A cold-blooded vertebrate animal that lives in water, moving with the help of fins and breathing with gills.
definitions.PLAY: Activity for amusement only, especially among the young.
definitions.GARDEN: An outdoor area containing one or more types of plants, usually plants grown for food or ornamental purposes.
definitions.TRAVEL: The act of traveling; passage from place to place.
definitions.MOVIE: A recorded sequence of images displayed on a screen at a rate sufficiently fast to create the appearance of motion.
definitions.MUSIC: A series of sounds organized in time, employing melody, harmony, tempo etc. usually to convey a mood.
definitions.BAND: A strip of material used for strengthening or coupling.
definitions.DRUM: A percussive musical instrument spanned with a thin covering on at least one end for striking, forming an acoustic chamber, affecting what materials are used to make it; a membranophone.
definitions.PIANO: A percussive keyboard musical instrument, usually ranging over seven octaves, with white and black colored keys, played by pressing these keys, causing hammers to strike strings.
definitions.GUITAR: A stringed musical instrument, of European origin, usually with a fretted fingerboard and six strings, played with the fingers or a plectrum (guitar pick).
definitions.CHESS: A board game for two players with each beginning with sixteen chess pieces moving according to fixed rules across a chessboard with the objective to checkmate the opposing king.
definitions.DICE: Gaming with one or more dice.
definitions.PUZZLE: Anything that is difficult to understand or make sense of.
definitions.HOBBY: An activity that one enjoys doing in one's spare time.
definitions.BUILD: The physique of a human body; constitution or structure of a human body.
definitions.SHOP: An establishment that sells goods or services to the public.
definitions.STUDY: (usually academic) To review materials already learned in order to make sure one does not forget them, usually in preparation for an examination.
definitions.TEACH: To show (someone) the way; to guide, conduct; to point, indicate.
definitions.HELP: Action given to provide assistance; aid.
definitions.SERVE: An act of putting the ball or shuttlecock in play in various games.
definitions.LIVE: To be alive; to have life.
definitions.GROW: To become larger, to increase in magnitude.
definitions.BE: A prefix, originally the same word as by.
definitions.SKETCH: A rapidly executed freehand drawing that is not intended as a finished work, often consisting of a multitude of overlapping lines.
definitions.POTTERY: Fired ceramic wares that contain clay when formed.
definitions.WEAVE: A type or way of weaving.
definitions.QUILT: A bed covering consisting of two layers of fabric stitched together, with insulation between, often having a decorative design.
definitions.SCRAPBOOK: A book, similar to a notebook or journal, in which personal or family memorabilia and photos are collected and arranged.
definitions.JOURNAL: A diary or daily record of a person, organization, vessel etc.; daybook.
definitions.POETRY: Literature composed in verse or language exhibiting conscious attention to patterns and rhythm.
definitions.MAGIC: The application of rituals or actions, especially those based on occult knowledge, to subdue or manipulate natural or supernatural beings and forces in order to have some benefit from them.
definitions.CIRCUS: A traveling company of performers that may include acrobats, clowns, trained animals, and other novelty acts, that gives shows usually in a circular tent.
definitions.YOGA: Any of several Hindu or Buddhist disciplines aimed at training the consciousness for a state of perfect spiritual insight and tranquillity.
definitions.PILATES: A physical fitness system developed in the early 20th century by Joseph Pilates.
definitions.KARATE: An Okinawan martial art involving primarily punching and kicking, but additionally, advanced throws, arm bars, grappling and all means of fighting.
definitions.TENNIS: A sport played by two players (or four in doubles), who alternately strike the ball over a net using racquets.
definitions.GOLF: A ball game played by individuals competing against one another in which the object is to hit a ball into each of a series of (usually 18 or nine) holes in the minimum number of strokes.
definitions.HOCKEY: Ice hockey, a game on ice in which two teams of six players skate and try to score by shooting a puck into the opposing team's net, using their sticks.
definitions.SKATING: To move along a surface (ice or ground) using skates.
definitions.SURFING: To ride a wave, usually on a surfboard.
definitions.SAILING: To be impelled or driven forward by the action of wind upon sails, as a ship on water.
definitions.ROWING: To propel (a boat or other craft) over water using oars.
definitions.DRIVING: To provide an impetus for motion or other physical change, to move an object by means of the provision of force thereto.
definitions.RACING: To take part in a race (in the sense of a contest).
definitions.RIDING: To transport oneself by sitting on and directing a horse, later also a bicycle etc.
definitions.WALKING: To move on the feet by alternately setting each foot (or pair or group of feet, in the case of animals with four or more feet) forward, with at least one foot on the ground at all times.
definitions.STARGAZE: To look at the stars at night.
definitions.COINS: (money) A piece of currency, usually metallic and in the shape of a disc, but sometimes polygonal, or with a hole in the middle.
definitions.STAMPS: An act of stamping the foot, paw or hoof.
definitions.ANTIQUE: A grotesque representation of a figure; a gargoyle.
definitions.ROASTING: To cook food by heating in an oven or over a fire without covering, resulting in a crisp, possibly even slightly charred appearance.
definitions.BREWING: To make tea or coffee by mixing tea leaves or coffee beans with hot water.
definitions.TASTING: A small amount of food or drink.
definitions.FARMING: To work on a farm, especially in the growing and harvesting of crops.
definitions.ROBOTS: A machine built to carry out some complex task or group of tasks by physically moving, especially one which can be programmed.
definitions.DRONES: A male ant, bee or wasp, which does not work but can fertilize the queen bee.
definitions.MODELING: To display for others to see, especially in regard to wearing clothing while performing the role of a fashion model.
definitions.RIDDLES: A verbal puzzle, mystery, or other problem of an intellectual nature.
definitions.ORIGAMI: The Japanese art of paper folding.
definitions.CALLIGRAPHY: The art or practice of writing letters and words in a decorative style; the letters and words so written.
definitions.JEWELRY: Collectively, personal ornamentation such as rings, necklaces, brooches and bracelets, made of precious metals and sometimes set with gemstones.
